the use of the platinum electrode for the measurement of nonstoichiometry in transition metal oxides can lead to erroneous values if the oxygen potential is high.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solubility is a function of the oxygen pressure and the temperature and the solubility increases with increasing oxygen pressure.
the solubility in the platinum of a transition metal oxide is a function of the oxygen partial pressure.
the thermodynamic calculations are in good agreement with experimental measurements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxygen partial pressure at which the oxide is stoichiometric depends on the oxygen partial pressure of the surrounding atmosphere and not the oxygen fugacity.
the nonstoichiometry of oxides can be measured with great accuracy using the solid state electrochemical method, provided that the solubility in the metal electrode is known.
the solubility limit for platinum in the transition metal oxide is not a fixed value but is a function of the oxygen partial pressure.
